result:
No failures, pre-existing warnings only (unrelated controllers with no test files).

I fixed the bug in `app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts:update()`: it was building a raw `Response` with a hardcoded `status: 302` redirect instead of using the framework's `this.redirect()` helper. A 302 on a PUT request causes the browser to replay the redirect as PUT again against `/posts/:id`, producing an infinite PUT loop (`ERR_TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS`) even though the update itself had already succeeded — while `store()` (POST → `this.redirect()`, which defaults to 303 for non-GET) worked fine. The fix replaces the raw `Response` with `return this.redirect(`/posts/${post.id}`)`, matching the pattern used elsewhere in the controller. I also added `tests/PostController.update.test.ts` covering both the successful-save redirect (asserts a 303 redirect to the post page) and that validation errors still return 422. `bun run typecheck`, `bun test` (4 pass, 0 fail), and `bunx guren check` (0 failures) all pass.
